Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
On Sat, 26 Jul 2003 01:08:32 GMT, rai...@mich.com wrote:

>Well the final round must have been over for an hour now.

Over for more than a day now.

>I'm waiting patiently for some word, any word, on how the event played
>out.

Not very patiently, evidently.

>You would think that with a delay this long we moved back into the
>dark ages!

Indeed.

There were 80 qualified players in attendance and playing on Saturday.
There were 13 more players that played in the Shadow Twin event.

Brian Moritz of Seattle, Washington took the win with a Tremere
intercept/bleed deck with 1.5 vps in the final.

Jay Kristoff also had 1.5 vps with an al AUS all the time deck, but
Brian had the higher ranking going into the finals.

Ben Spaulding had .5 vps for third place with a Brujah Princes
Remembering Carthage deck..

Forrest Nielson took fourth place with the Toreador Antitribu /
Daughters of Cacophony (Siren's Lure) bleed deck that won the
Washington, D. C. qualifier.

Jean-Francois Caron took fifth place with a new Gangrel bleed/toolbox
deck.

Congratulations to all involved.

Carpe noctem.

Lasombra

The Lasombra <TheLa...@hotmail.com> wrote in message news:<ts89ivcvqmmbdml8g...@4ax.com>...

> On Sat, 26 Jul 2003 01:08:32 GMT, rai...@mich.com wrote:
>
>

> Forrest Nielsen took fourth place with the Toreador Antitribu /

> Daughters of Cacophony (Siren's Lure) bleed deck that won the
> Washington, D. C. qualifier.
>

Actually, it was a Daughters of Cacophony deck, titled "Lost Girls
Just Wanna Have Fun".

The Toreador anti were only a support clan. The deck has 6 Daughters
(2x Angela Preston, 2x Gael Pilet, Deliliah Monroe, and Celeste), 5
!Toreador (2x Jost Warner, 2x Shelia Mezarin, 1x Mercy), and 1 Caitiff
(Maldavis).

For the DC qualifier, it was an even split of Daughters and !Toreador,
because Anarch were not yet legal. On the other hand, this deck (with
minor changes) also went to the finals in the Baltimore Storyline held
in Baltimore as a Daughters of Cacophony (9+3) deck in January 2002.
